description: Closed vocabulary for the look of a screen. Agents tag each screenshot with one page type, the sections it shows, one to three styles, one density, and one or two kinds of imagery. Color mode, fonts, colors, and radius come from the computed CSS, not from this vocabulary.

page_types.description: Use a surface slug from taxonomy/surfaces.json. Use not-a-page for an asset, pattern, shader, slide, or mockup that is not a web or app screen. Use other for a screen that matches no surface.

density.name: Airy
density.definition: Few elements and wide empty space; one idea per view.

density.name: Balanced
density.definition: A normal amount of content with clear space between groups.

density.name: Dense
density.definition: Many elements packed close: data screens, long navigation, many cards or links in one view.

imagery.name: Photography
imagery.definition: Real photos of people, places, or products.

imagery.name: Illustration
imagery.definition: Drawn or vector artwork, characters, or spot illustrations.

imagery.name: 3D render
imagery.definition: Rendered 3D objects or scenes, including WebGL.

imagery.name: Product UI
imagery.definition: Screenshots or mockups of the product's own interface, or the interface itself.

imagery.name: Abstract graphic
imagery.definition: Gradients, shapes, blobs, lines, or generative art with no subject.

imagery.name: Pattern or texture
imagery.definition: Repeating patterns, noise, grain, or material textures as the main visual.

imagery.name: Icons
imagery.definition: Icons or logos are the main visuals.

imagery.name: Type only
imagery.definition: No images; text and color carry the screen.

styles.name: Minimal
styles.definition: Very few elements, a restrained palette, and generous whitespace.

styles.name: Clean SaaS
styles.definition: The current software-company default: neutral sans type, product screenshots, soft borders or subtle gradients, rounded cards.

styles.name: Corporate
styles.definition: Conventional enterprise look: stock photos, safe blue or gray palette, many links and calls to action.

styles.name: Editorial
styles.definition: A magazine or newspaper layout led by typography and text columns.

styles.name: Swiss grid
styles.definition: International typographic style: a strict visible grid, sans type, strong hierarchy, flat color fields.

styles.name: Brutalist
styles.definition: Raw and unpolished on purpose: default-looking type, exposed boxes and borders, harsh contrast, little decoration.

styles.name: Neo-brutalist
styles.definition: Thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat saturated fills, and chunky type.

styles.name: Typographic
styles.definition: Oversized type is the main visual; images are absent or secondary.

styles.name: Luxury
styles.definition: Refined and premium: thin or serif type, muted or dark palette, large photography, slow pacing.

styles.name: Playful
styles.definition: Bright, rounded, and friendly: mascots, stickers, bouncy shapes, informal copy.

styles.name: Hand-drawn
styles.definition: Sketchy strokes, doodles, scribbles, or handwriting fonts.

styles.name: Retro
styles.definition: Imitates an earlier era of print or design, such as the 1960s to 1980s.

styles.name: Y2K
styles.definition: Late 1990s and early 2000s digital look: chrome, bubbles, glossy gradients, early web graphics.

styles.name: Pixel
styles.definition: Pixel art, bitmap fonts, and low-resolution game graphics.

styles.name: Terminal
styles.definition: Looks like a command line or code editor: monospace type, prompts, ASCII art.

styles.name: Dark glow
styles.definition: A dark interface with glowing gradients, neon accents, and spotlight effects, common on developer tools.

styles.name: Gradient mesh
styles.definition: Large soft multi-color gradients, aurora, or mesh blurs as the main backdrop.

styles.name: Glassmorphism
styles.definition: Frosted translucent panels with background blur over color.

styles.name: Neumorphism
styles.definition: Soft extruded and inset shapes made from same-color shadows.

styles.name: Skeuomorphic
styles.definition: Imitates real materials and objects: paper, leather, metal, realistic controls.

styles.name: 3D immersive
styles.definition: 3D scenes or WebGL objects dominate the screen and create depth.

styles.name: Image-led
styles.definition: Full-bleed photography or imagery dominates; text sits on or around it.

styles.name: Collage
styles.definition: Layered cutouts, mixed media, and overlapping elements like a scrapbook.

styles.name: Maximalist
styles.definition: Loud and full: many colors, patterns, type sizes, and elements at once.

styles.name: Monochrome
styles.definition: Black, white, and grays, with at most one accent hue.

styles.name: Pastel
styles.definition: Soft, light, low-saturation colors.

styles.name: Vibrant
styles.definition: Saturated, high-energy colors used across large areas.

styles.name: Organic
styles.definition: Earthy tones, natural textures, and soft irregular shapes.

styles.name: Futuristic
styles.definition: Science-fiction or HUD look: technical lines, grids, readouts, cyber accents.

styles.name: Textured
styles.definition: Grain, noise, or paper texture laid over flat color.
